newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian opposition hopes for UK Labour support.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian opposition hopes for UK Labour support.

text.p: Nigeria's opposition on Friday hailed the outcome of Britain's general election, saying they expected a Labour government to take a firmer stand against General Sani Abacha's government on democracy and human rights.

"We have no doubt that Labour will make life hell for the military government because traditionally it has always sided with the oppressed," said Gani Fawehinmi, a leading dissident who heads the National Conscience Party (NCP).

"The human rights community believes Labour will be less ambivalent on Nigeria than the Conservative government has been," said Clement Nwankwo, head of the Constitutional Rights Project, which campaigns against human rights abuse in Nigeria.

The West imposed sanctions on military-ruled Nigeria over the annulment of a 1993 election meant to restore democracy, and the later hanging of nine minority rights activists including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa.
But opposition activists consider the sanctions token and have always blamed former colonial power Britain for not leading its Western partners to take a tougher line.

"With the Conservatives out of power the military have lost an ally," said Fawehinmi, adding: "We expect the new British government to take the lead within the European Union in isolating the Abacha regime."
"We see them taking action such as freezing assets of those against democracy in Nigeria and tightening the rules about entry into the EU of members of the regime," said Nwankwo.

Later this year heads of government from the Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies are due to review Nigeria's suspension from the organisation following Saro-Wiwa's execution and discuss whether further measures are needed.
Government spokesmen were not immediately available to comment on the outcome of the British election, which state radio reported without comment.
